reviewer_role: TC perspective; not independent final approval
decision: Do not treat this review as approval to execute G6. The test inventory and acceptance-scope boundaries are reviewable, but the Node invocation and inventory source need clarification in a revised contract.

findings.topic: Node option placement and exact inventory provenance
findings.evidence: package.json defines test as `node --test tests/*.test.mjs`. Contract G6.2 invokes `npm test -- --test-concurrency=2 --test-reporter=spec`, which npm appends after the package-script arguments. The contract does not establish that Node 24 parses these flags in that position or that they control concurrency/reporting. It also says compare names to the accepted B01 inventory without pinning the historical log/parser artifact that defines the exact 387 names.
findings.required_resolution: Revise the contract to specify an unambiguous Node argv ordering (or a dedicated fixed runner) and pin the accepted B01 spec-log bytes/parser rule used to derive the exact expected 387 test names. Retain all 387 callbacks, the 30-second per-callback ceiling and 180-second command ceiling; no waiver or filtering.
findings.verification_scope: Static contract review only; no test command was run.

findings.evidence: The contract records two accepted aggregate callbacks above 30 seconds under default concurrency (36.5726s and 34.6788s). Concurrency 2 is a scheduling hypothesis, not evidence that all callbacks meet the unchanged 30-second ceiling.
findings.required_resolution: Keep the gate fail-closed if any of the exact 387 callbacks exceeds 30 seconds. Report the actual per-callback durations; do not increase thresholds, skip, split, or replace callbacks.

findings.evidence: The matrix explicitly identifies implemented authentication, job, command-status, and workspace evidence while listing absent plan-decision, human-submission, controls, release-manifest, approval, events, artifacts, notifications, bridge/device and runtime-event routes. It also leaves original AT-01..AT-32 unexecuted and AT-21 partial.
findings.required_resolution: Preserve these limitations in G6/G7 reporting. G1-G5 regression or a passing 202/job/workspace test must not be presented as worker execution, artifact/log/image/device isolation, corporate SSO, or original AT completion.

findings.topic: Python regression reuse and split command limits
findings.evidence: G6.1 calls the accepted G5 orchestrator for fresh G1-G5 execution and targeted B01 Node regressions. The contract identifies separate Python subprocess ceilings and records that prior G5 evidence is not substituted for fresh execution.
findings.required_resolution: The revised runner must preserve exact case inventories, zero skips, child lifecycle cleanup, and each accepted command ceiling; the split must not omit or duplicate tests silently.
